prs.title: Mirror Hyprland triangular corners in shell surfaces
prs.body: Mirror Hyprland triangular corners in shell surfaces The shell already mirrors Hyprland's `decoration:rounding` as `Style.cornerRadius`, but it ignores `decoration:rounding_power`. Themes that use `rounding_power = 1.0` (Hyprland's triangular corner) get 45° cut window corners, while every shell surface still draws round corners. This makes `BorderSurface` follow the window corner shape: - `Style` also reads `decoration:rounding_power`, the same way it reads `decoration:rounding`, and sets `cornerChamfer` when the value is 1.0 or less. - `BorderGeometry` gains a `chamfer` flag. prs.title: Retry delay inhibit after logind OperationInProgress on resume
prs.body: ## Why `omarchy-sleep-lock.service` is `Restart=always`. After suspend/resume, logind still treats the previous delay inhibit as in progress, so `systemd-inhibit --mode=delay` fails with: ``` Failed to inhibit: The operation inhibition has been requested for is already running ``` (logind `OperationInProgress` / sd-bus `EINPROGRESS`). The unit then logs FAILURE every wake, churns restarts, and does not hold a delay inhibit for the *next* suspend. Closes #13160. ## Change Probe with a throwaway `systemd-inhibit ... true`, retrying only that "already running" error (up to ~6s), then `exec` the real inhibitor so `systemd-inhibit` remains the unit main PID and monitor stderr stays on the journal. Unrelated inhibit failures still fail the unit immediately. ## Tests `test/shell.d/sleep-monitor-test.sh` covers: - retry until the third probe succeeds, then final `exec` (4 calls) - unrelated inhibit errors fail after one call (call count asserted) Base: quattro. prs.title: Use the KeyboardPanel focus pattern on the full-screen overlays
prs.body: ## Use the KeyboardPanel focus pattern on the full-screen overlays The overlays take keyboard focus exclusively: ```qml WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive ``` Hyprland routes every pointer and touch event to a surface with exclusive focus before hit-testing anything above it. So a surface drawn on top of an overlay cannot be touched. The event goes to the overlay underneath, which treats it as a click outside and dismisses itself. Omarchy already knows this. `Ui/KeyboardPanel.qml` says so: > Exclusive would also grant map-time focus, but it makes Hyprland route *every* pointer event to the exclusive surface no matter which output the cursor is over, which leaves clicks on any other monitor unable to reach the dismissal surfaces below. And it already has the fix: ```qml WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: open ? (focusPrimed ? WlrKeyboardFocus.OnDemand : WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive) : WlrKeyboardFocus.None ``` Prime with Exclusive so focus is acquired when the surface maps, settle on OnDemand 75ms later, which releases compositor-wide hit-testing. prs.title: Let omarchy-hyprland-focus-app focus an exact window by address
prs.body: `omarchy-hyprland-focus-app` matches by application identity, which can't tell one window of an app from another. With nine kitty windows open, a caller that knows *which* terminal it means (a notification raised by a specific window, a plugin, a script) still lands on whichever one the search reaches first. prs.title: Keep the bluetooth widget on the bar when the radio is blocked
prs.body: ## Problem On hardware where the Bluetooth rfkill switch is a **platform** switch, turning Bluetooth off removes the Bluetooth widget from the bar — including the control that turns it back on. The radio cannot be re-enabled from the GUI at all; recovery requires dropping to a terminal. `omarchy-bluetooth-power off` turns the radio off with `rfkill block bluetooth`, which is deliberate and correct — it is the half of the state that survives a reboot. But on a platform switch, blocking does not merely clear BlueZ's `Powered`: it **cuts power to the radio**. The controller leaves the USB bus, `hci0` disappears, BlueZ drops the adapter, and `Bluetooth.defaultAdapter` becomes `null`. `shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml` gated the whole widget on that object: ```qml visible: adapter !== null ``` so the widget disappeared with the adapter, and `Bar.qml` collapsed the slot to zero width (`implicitWidth: activeItem && activeItem.visible ? ... : 0`). The panel already has the states this needs — a `󰂲` off glyph and a "Turned Off" label, both keyed on `!adapter.enabled`. On this hardware those branches are simply **unreachable**, because the adapter object is gone rather than disabled.

prs.body: ## Problem The bar's workspace indicator sometimes freezes and stops following workspace switches. Hyprland itself is fine (`hyprctl activeworkspace` is correct); only the shell is stale, and it stays that way until `omarchy restart shell`. prs.title: Document Lua bind dispatch and new plugin install steps in agent skill
prs.body: The agent skill under \`default/agents/skills/omarchy/\` was missing two things an agent needs to act correctly: - **hyprland.md**: it didn't say that \`hyprctl -j binds\` reports an \`o.bind(...)\` binding as dispatcher \`__lua\` with an opaque numeric handle in \`arg\`, not \`exec\` plus the command. This matters for a tool that installs its own plugin. Both verified on Omarchy 4.0.4-1: all 240 binds report \`__lua\`, and the plugin command syntax was checked against \`bin/omarchy-plugin-validate\`, \`bin/omarchy-plugin-enable\`, and \`bin/omarchy-plugin-add\`. prs.title: Retry bt-agent after bluetooth.service instead of skipping
prs.body: ## Problem `bt-agent.service` used `ExecCondition=systemctl is-active bluetooth.service`. When that condition fails, systemd **skips** the unit. A skip is terminal for that activation — `Restart=on-failure` does not try again — so a race with bluez at login (or after `systemctl restart bluetooth`) leaves the session with **no pairing agent**. The radio still scans; pairing never completes. Reported in #13247 with journal evidence (`Skipped due to 'exec-condition'` until bluetoothd is already up). ## Change - Wait for `bluetooth.service` **inside `ExecStart`**, then `exec bt-agent`, so a late bluez is no longer a terminal skip and the Type=simple start job does not hold `graphical-session.target`. - Add `After=graphical-session.target` (same pattern as migrate-notify) so the unit cannot pin the session target open. - Do **not** add user-manager `After=`/`Wants=` on system `bluetooth.service` (those deps are inert in the user manager). - Keep `ConditionPathIsDirectory=/sys/class/bluetooth` so machines with no Bluetooth class still skip cleanly. - Update `systemd-test.sh` with directive-anchored assertions for the wait + ordering. ## Test - `ROOT=... bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh`

prs.title: Force DPMS enable on system wake when status is stale
prs.body: ## What `omarchy-brightness-display on` skips the DPMS enable when every enabled monitor already reports `dpmsStatus=true`. That avoids an extra modeset flash on the lock screen, but on NVIDIA s2idle resume Hyprland can report that status while the panel is still dark, so the skip leaves the laptop black until a hard reboot. `--force` bypasses the guard. `omarchy-system-wake` uses it (lock-screen input, auth, cancelled idle — not a dedicated resume hook). prs.body: Fixes #13297. On MacBookPro14,1, BCM4350's default hybrid coexistence policy interrupts A2DP audio while 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is connected. prs.title: Honor D-Bus idle inhibits on the paths Chromium actually calls
prs.body: Fixes #6475. Quattro replaced hypridle with the Quickshell idle service. hypridle owned `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver`; nothing does now, so D-Bus `Inhibit()` from browsers and players is dropped and the screensaver fires over playing video. ## What this does `omarchy-idle-inhibit` owns `org.freedesktop.ScreenSaver` (the same name hypridle owned) and exports the object paths clients actually call: - **`/org/freedesktop/ScreenSaver`** — Chromium/Chrome `power_save_blocker_linux.cc` (video / display wake lock) - **`/ScreenSaver`** — VLC, Firefox/Zen `org.freedesktop.PowerManagement` is left unowned. prs.title: Keep a legacy Windows VM password with $$ working after the Quattro migration
prs.body: Upgrading a 3.x install to Quattro moves the Windows VM's compose from `~/.config/windows/docker-compose.yml` to the root-owned one, and `migrate_legacy_compose` carries the password across by reading the raw text between the quotes. That text is what Docker Compose parsed, and Compose turns `$$` into a single `$`, so a legacy password written as `a$$b` was set in the guest as `a$b`. Migration kept `a$$b`: it saved that as the RDP password and then escaped it again for the new compose. The guest's disk is preserved, so Windows keeps `a$b`, and every RDP login after the upgrade fails. This decodes `$$` to `$` as the password is read, so both the RDP credentials and the new compose hold the password the guest actually has. A legacy password with a lone `$` (`pa$`, `a$!b`) is unchanged, as before. One whose `$` was followed by a name (`pa$word`) was already cut short by Compose when the VM was installed, and the original cannot be reconstructed, so that case stays as it is. prs.body: ## Summary When a panel widget's or plugin's `close()` method throws an exception (such as a cloned plugin referencing an outdated/modified property or encountering a runtime error), the unhandled exception halts `close()` before `root.open = false` can execute. prs.title: List submap bindings under the chord that enters their mode in the keybindings menu
prs.body: A bind scoped to a submap only fires inside its mode, but `omarchy-menu-keybindings` lists it as an always-on global chord. On my config, `SUPER + P` enters a window mode whose binds render like this: ``` ESCAPE → Leave window mode H → Shrink width J → Grow height L → Grow width SHIFT + H → Swap left ``` The `ESC` fire, but `ESCAPE → Leave window mode` reads like a shortcut I can press right now, and none of these rows say what they belong to or where they come from. These report dispatcher `__lua`, and the menu already recovers the dispatch from the Lua bind cache, which holds the evaluated argument — so the entry bind to a mode is in there, just never used. ### Fix - Carry each bind's `submap:` field through the emit stage. - Build a map from a submap name to the chord that enters it, sourced from both roads

prs.title: Add recursion guard to omarchy-mise-install wrappers
prs.body: ## Summary When a tool is not installed or mise fails to provide the requested binary, `mise x <tool> -- <bin>` falls back to searching `PATH`. Because the wrapper itself is installed in `~/.local/bin`, mise re-executes the wrapper script. Without a recursion guard, this creates an unbounded fork loop (~1,000 forks/sec) that saturates the machine until it exhausts process limits. This emits a tool-specific environment guard variable (`_OMARCHY_MISE_GUARD_<COMMAND>`) at the top of the generated wrapper so recursive invocations fail fast with exit code 127 and a clear stderr message instead of hanging the machine. prs.title: Document the hardware clock convention for dual boot
prs.body: ## Summary On a dual-boot machine, Windows keeps the hardware clock in local time while Linux reads it as UTC. After a Windows session Omarchy briefly comes up with a clock skewed by the UTC offset until NTP corrects it — and a snapshot taken in that window (e.g. the pre-update one from `omarchy update`) carries a future timestamp, so limine-snapper-sync adds no Limine menu entry for later snapshots until real time passes it (#13367). The upstream sync-side report is linked in the issue. This closes the issue's documentation option: the dual-boot manual said nothing about the clock, so it now explains the mismatch, the snapshot-menu symptom, and both conventions — making Windows read UTC (`RealTimeIsUniversal`, recommended) or making Linux read local time (`timedatectl set-local-rtc 1`) — with a `timedatectl` verification step. Fixes #13367 ## Testing Docs-only change; no test surface. Verified against the issue's reproduction description and `timedatectl`'s own output labels.

prs.title: omarchy-refresh-config shouldn't override symlinked file content
prs.body: When a file under `~/.config` is a symlink — a dotfile managed by GNU stow, say — `omarchy-refresh-config` writes the Omarchy default through the link. `cp -f` follows the destination, so the user's own file at the link target is overwritten, and the backup it saves is a copy of that file's content rather than the link. The user's `.bak` does hold their old content, but the dotfile they manage elsewhere has been clobbered without being told. This carries @J3rome's fix across to `quattro`: - The backup is taken with `cp -d`, so a symlinked config is backed up as the symlink. - A symlinked config is replaced with `cp --remove-destination`, so the link is swapped for a regular file holding the default and its target is left alone. - A regular config is still overwritten in place with `cp -f`, as on `quattro` today, so it keeps its mode and any hard links. Recreating every file would have turned a `0600` config into a `0644` one. - The comparison runs first and nothing is backed up or copied when the config already matches the default; `cmp` follows symlinks, so a link to identical content is left as a link. `test/shell.d/refresh-config-test.sh` now covers a stowed config (target untou

prs.title: Support double-press actions in Hyprland bindings
prs.body: Adds optional double-press actions to `o.bind` and `o.rebind`, allowing two actions on one shortcut without custom timer logic. ```lua o.rebind("SUPER + K", "My shortcut", "single-command", { double_press = "double-command", timeout = 250, }) ``` The first press waits 250 ms by default. prs.title: Stamp new migrations with wall-clock time
prs.body: ## Why `omarchy-dev-add-migration` named files after `git log -1 --format=%cd --date=unix`. Every branch cut from the same commit therefore received the same migration id. The runner records that id as done, so a later migration with the colliding name never runs. Reported in #13516 (observed collision on `1789095456` from the quattro merge of #11263). ## What Use wall-clock `date +%s` instead of HEAD's committer date. Claim the path with `noclobber` / O_EXCL create and bump the id until the create succeeds, so concurrent runs in one checkout cannot mint the same file. Does not rewrite existing migrations. Merge-time uniqueness against history is still a useful follow-up; this only stops the helper from minting the same id on sibling branches (and tightens same-tree races). ## Test ``` bash test/shell.d/dev-add-migration-test.sh bash test/shell.d/dev-add-migration-race-test.sh ``` Note: #13656 targets the same helper lines (with a test). Happy to coordinate / close if maintainers prefer that PR. Refs #13516

prs.title: Re-probe night light after each minute so the bar follows hyprsunset's schedule
prs.body: Fixes #8286. The night light service asks hyprsunset for its temperature once at startup and again after an Omarchy toggle, but hyprsunset also switches on its own: the stock `hyprsunset.conf` profiles at 07:00 and 20:00. Nothing tells the shell about those, so the indicator keeps the state it last saw. On my laptop the shell started in the afternoon, the 20:00 profile applied while the lid was shut, and the bar showed night light off all evening under a 4000K screen. In the morning it goes the other way, and clicking the indicator then toggles to the side the screen is already on. hyprsunset has no change events (its socket only answers requests), so the service has to ask. It now probes again a second past every wall-clock minute. hyprsunset lands scheduled switches exactly on the minute, so the bar follows within about a second. A switch due while suspended applies within a minute of wake, and the next probe catches it. A probe is skipped while a toggle is still being applied, so it can't overwrite the optimistic state with the old temperature. `test/shell.d/nightlight-test.sh` gains two cases for the minute alignment. prs.title: Keep other systems' boot entries through a factory reset
prs.body: Fixes #13689. On a machine whose ESP is shared with other systems, a factory reset removed their Limine entries twice: once while staging (`omarchy-system-factory-reset`), and again on the first boot after it (`omarchy-provision-owner`). Both rewrote `limine.conf` from the template and deleted every other machine-id directory the file listed. - **Staging:** the global settings still start over from the template, but every entry is kept. Only this installation's entry is emptied and re-keyed to the new machine-id, and only the replaced machine-id's directory is removed. `limine-update` then refills the entry in place. Other systems' entries now survive, and a stale one of theirs shouldn't block the reset. - **First boot:** another system's machine-id no longer counts as stale. prs.title: Stop mistaking the T2 chip for an Apple GPU in Vulkan detection
prs.body: Fixes #13727 ## Summary - The Vulkan driver detection matched `(VGA|Display).*Apple` against `lspci`. `VGA` matches inside `Non-VGA`, so the T2 chip (`Non-VGA unclassified device: Apple Inc. T2 Bridge Controller`) made every T2 Mac install `vulkan-asahi`, the Apple Silicon GPU driver. - The match is now anchored on the lspci class name (`^\S+ (VGA compatible controller|Display controller): `), which keeps the existing VGA/Display semantics and just stops matching `Non-VGA`. This covers all three copies of the pattern: `install/hardware/vulkan.sh`, `migrations/1784401744.sh` and `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. - A new migration removes `vulkan-asahi` from x86_64 installs, where it can never drive a GPU. It only runs when `pacman -Rs --print` shows the removal is clean, so it never breaks a package that relies on it as its only Vulkan driver. Apple Silicon installs are left alone. This overlaps with the sysfs rewrites in #12076, #11259 and #12681, which would fix `vulkan.sh` for fresh installs. It's kept deliberately small so it can land independently or be folded into whichever of those merges first. The upgrade-script fix and the cleanup migration aren't covered by any of them. #

prs.title: move screen recording from `Alt + Print Screen` to preserve SysRq keys
prs.body: ## Brief The default `Alt + Print Screen` screen-recording binding conflicts with Linux Magic SysRq, which uses the same chord as the prefix for emergency and diagnostic commands. SysRq can help recover from an unresponsive system and inspect or debug kernel state during crashes and it is quite an important Linux feature. ## Config Unless the key chord is actually available, then this would be naught; but if so, then here's how you configure them to access more commands. The available commands can be restricted through the kernel.sysrq sysctl: 0 disables keyboard access, 1 enables every command, and a bitmask enables selected categories such as diagnostic dumps, filesystem sync, read-only remounting, process signaling, or reboot. See the [Linux kernel SysRq documentation]( ## Solution Move screen recording to `Ctrl + Print Screen`. The Hyprland binding-conflicts test passes.

prs.title: Stop mise wrappers recursing when mise's activation variables are missing
prs.body: A wrapper from `omarchy-mise-install` ends in `exec mise x <package> -- <bin>`, and `mise x` looks `<bin>` up by name. It puts the directories it added ahead of the rest of PATH, and it knows which those are from the variables `mise activate` exports (`__MISE_DIFF`). A process that starts a wrapper with an activated PATH but a reduced environment (a service, a sandbox, or a launcher that passes only a safe set of variables) leaves those out. `mise x` then treats the package's directory as an ordinary entry behind `~/.local/bin`, finds the wrapper again, and the wrapper runs itself until something kills it, holding a CPU core the whole time. This is the same loop #3685's fix addressed for `exec "$bin"`; `mise x` still reaches it through this path. **Reproduction** (on a machine with the `gh` wrapper installed): ```bash PATH_ACTIVE=$(bash -lic 'printf %s "$PATH"') env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH_ACTIVE" timeout 8 ~/.local/bin/gh --version; echo "exit=$?" # exit=124: the wrapper loops until the timeout ``` With this change the same command prints the gh version at once. **Change** - The wrapper resolves the bin inside the package's install with `mise which --tool <package> <bin>` and

prs.title: Reveal Dropbox files through org.freedesktop.FileManager1
prs.body: The Dropbox panel opens a recent file with a hardcoded `nautilus --select`, so anyone using a different file manager gets Nautilus anyway. It's the only place in the shell panels that names Nautilus directly. This sends `ShowItems` to `org.freedesktop.FileManager1` over D-Bus instead. That call means "reveal this file, selected", and Nautilus, Dolphin, Thunar, Nemo and others all implement it, so the file opens in whichever file manager owns that bus name. Nautilus is in the base package set and ships `/usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.freedesktop.FileManager1.service`, so a stock install still reveals the file in Nautilus. prs.body: With an external monitor connected and the laptop lid closed, logging out can suspend the machine before SDDM has finished starting. logind counts enabled DRM outputs when deciding whether the laptop is docked, so compositor teardown or DPMS can temporarily defeat `HandleLidSwitchDocked=ignore` even though the display remains physically connected. The system service holds only a `handle-lid-switch` inhibitor while Omarchy's physical-connector detector finds an external monitor and the configured docked policy is `ignore`. Explicit suspend and idle policy remain available. - `Type=notify` and `NotifyAccess=all` delay display-manager startup until readiness; docked startup reports readiness only after acquisition succeeds. prs.title: Keep an early polkit Enter and submit it in the background when PAM asks
prs.body: The polkit dialog shows its password field as soon as a request starts, but PAM only asks for the password once `polkit-agent-helper-1` is running. The keypress is dropped without any feedback, the password is never sent, and users end up pressing Enter repeatedly. prs.title: Smooth out battery time
prs.body: ## Summary Two looks at the battery a few seconds apart now show the same hours. Before, those hours were the charge left divided by one short power sample, so a sample that doubled cut the hours in half while the battery barely moved. ## Why this estimate UPower sets time to empty to `3600 * energy / energy_rate` in [`src/up-device-battery.c`]( On a pack with about 65 Wh left, a sample moving from about 5.6 W to about 11 W moves the printed time from about 11 hours to about 6 hours. The battery did not lose half its charge. The replacement is the same relation, charge left divided by how fast charge is leaving, taken from the battery's own counter: - Between looks, `new = old × charge_now / charge_then`. An 11-hour reading (39600 seconds) at 6,000,000 µAh, after the counter falls to 5,997,000, is 39580 seconds, printed as 10h 59m. Half the charge left prints as 5h 30m. A power sample that says 3 hours, with the counter unmoved, changes this term by zero. Time asleep changes it by zero, because sleep did not remove charge. - A new rate is `charge_now × seconds / charge_used`, and only when the span is 60–180 seconds and the charge used is more than one counter step (1000 µAh). prs.title: Stop the dictation indicator from making voxtype run nvidia-smi
prs.body: ## Problem On hybrid laptops with the dGPU off, the bar's dictation indicator wakes the NVIDIA GPU and loads the NVIDIA driver every time the bar is built: at login, on shell restart, and on every resume. It runs twice each time, because `Indicators.qml` creates `Dictation` for both the horizontal and the vertical bar. The next suspend then hung and froze the laptop. ## Root cause `bin/omarchy-voxtype-status` runs `voxtype status --follow --extended --format json`. prs.title: Let PipeWire follow the source's sample rate
prs.body: Part 2 of the pro-audio proposal in #13832. Nothing changes for 48 kHz sources; 44.1, 88.2 and 96 kHz sources play at their own rate when the hardware supports it, and other rates are still resampled. ## Problem PipeWire's `clock.allowed-rates` is `[ 48000 ]` on a stock install, so every 44.1 kHz track and 88.2/96 kHz recording is resampled on its way to the device. It also applies the same rates to the running graph with `pw-metadata`, since PipeWire only reads `conf.d` at startup. So the change takes effect on update without restarting PipeWire or interrupting playback. prs.title: Mute crash toasts while diagnosis is in flight
prs.body: ## Summary Keep crash reproductions quiet for the lifetime of the diagnosis agent. The terminal runs a session wrapper that holds a per-program lock while the agent runs inline, rather than relying on a timestamp that can expire mid-investigation. Repeated clicks do not start a second diagnosis for the same program. Normal exits and agent failures release suppression immediately. The watcher retains lock files and never unlinks them, avoiding the race where cleanup deletes a fresh session's marker. The agent does not inherit the lock descriptor, so background harness children cannot prolong suppression. Storage or lock failures still allow diagnosis. ## Validation 40 focused shell checks pass, including an active session with an hour-old timestamp, repeated clicks, normal/failing agent exits, restarting a diagnosis, and unavailable runtime storage. Restoring the previous timestamp watcher or unlinking the active lock independently fails the lifecycle check. prs.title: Hold notification toasts back behind a fullscreen window

prs.title: Fix hot reload of local plugins by busting the component cache
prs.body: ## Problem Saving a file in a local plugin (`~/.config/omarchy/plugins/<id>/`) is supposed to hot-reload it, but the edited code never shows up until the whole shell is restarted with `omarchy-restart-shell`. The watcher side works: `inotifywait` reports the change and `reloadPlugins()` unloads and re-creates the plugin. But before re-creating it, `finishPluginReload()` tries to drop Qt's compiled-component cache with: ```qml if (typeof Qt.clearComponentCache === "function") Qt.clearComponentCache() ``` `clearComponentCache()` only exists on the C++ `QQmlEngine`. It is not part of the QML `Qt` object, so `typeof` is `"undefined"` and the call is silently skipped. Qt then serves the stale compiled component for the unchanged URL, so the reloaded plugin runs its old code. Fixes #6981 Fixes #9251 ## Fix Qt caches compiled components by URL. `PluginRegistry` now keeps a `codeGeneration` counter that `finishPluginReload()` bumps on every reload. `entryPointUrl()` appends it as a query string (`Panel.qml?v=3`) to entry points under the local plugins dir, so each reload asks Qt for a new URL and the edited file is compiled again. - Generation 0 (the first load) keeps the exact URLs used t

prs.title: Cap idle timeouts to the largest Qt Timer interval
prs.body: Fixes #13920 ## Summary Idle timeouts larger than a Qt `Timer` interval can hold overflowed. Qt then clamped the interval to 1 ms, and the shell logged a warning on every tick until the log filled `/run/user/$UID`. This PR caps the configured seconds at the largest value that still fits in an interval. ```diff +// Qt Timer intervals are signed 32-bit milliseconds. Anything larger wraps +// negative, Qt clamps it to 1 ms, and the shell logs a warning every tick. +var MAX_TIMER_SECONDS = Math.floor(2147483647 / 1000) + function secondsFromConfig(value, fallback) { var n = Number(value) if (!isFinite(n) || n < 0) return fallback - return Math.floor(n) + return Math.min(Math.floor(n), MAX_TIMER_SECONDS) } ``` `screensaver` and `lock` are both read through `secondsFromConfig`, so their delays, and the `lockDelaySeconds * 1000` interval computed from them, now stay within the int32 limit. ## Evidence `test/shell.d/idle-test.sh`: - **Before:** ``` expected: 2147483 actual: 999999999 not ok - idle caps seconds to the largest Timer interval ``` **After:** ``` ok - idle caps seconds to the largest Timer interval ok - idle keeps the largest Timer interval ok - idle seconds never overflow a Ti

prs.title: List commands moved into a group by metadata in fast-path group help
prs.body: `omarchy setup` and `omarchy setup --help` don't list `omarchy setup factory reset`, even though `omarchy commands --all` shows it and the route dispatches fine. ## Cause `bin/omarchy-system-factory-reset` joins the `setup` group through `# omarchy:group=setup`. prs.title: parseExecArgv accepts NUL, so the argv validated is not the argv executed
prs.body: ## Summary `parseExecArgv` is the only validator on the one path in the shell where a notification sender chooses what gets executed. It rejects a leading-dash program so `argv` cannot read it as an option, but that check reads `parsed[0].charAt(0)` and nothing else. `Util.execArgv` receives the JS string as a C string, so everything from the first NUL onward is invisible to `exec` — the validated string and the executed string are not the same string. The fix (`shell/plugins/notifications/NotificationLogic.js`) rejects any element containing a NUL, so what is checked is what runs: - A NUL after the program truncates the rest of the element — `exec` sees the prefix. - A leading NUL slips the dash check (`charAt(0)` reads the NUL, not the dash that follows) and leaves `exec` an empty program. ## Notes - **Not a privilege escalation.** Any session-bus process may set this hint by the freedesktop protocol's design, which is equivalent to same-uid code execution; #8433 tracks that boundary separately. This is a gate-integrity fix only. - **Persistence is not implicated.** `JSON.stringify` re-escapes the NUL, so popup files stay strict JSON and the argv round-trip is lossless. - Only NU

prs.title: omarchy-plugin-add: mv -T so a lost race fails instead of nesting
prs.body: ## Summary `bin/omarchy-plugin-add` does a check-then-act: it tests `[[ -e $target ]]` and then `mv "$stage" "$target"`. With plain `mv`, a target that appears between the two (a concurrent add) is treated as a directory to move *into* — `mv` exits 0 and nests the staged checkout inside it, leaving a corrupted plugin tree reported as success. `mv -T` makes the collision fail loudly instead. The failure path also drops the staged checkout (`rm -rf "$stage"`), so a lost race leaves no `.add.tmp.$$` behind, and the error message names the failure without asserting a single cause — a concurrent add, permissions, or disk space. ## Notes - **`omarchy-plugin-update` is not exposed to this.** It does an in-place `git fetch` + `merge --ff-only` on the existing checkout, so git's own `index.lock` already serialises concurrent updates. - **`flock` is deliberately out of scope.** It would make the contract explicit rather than dependent on how small the race window is, but it is a larger change. Worth a follow-up if the stronger guarantee is wanted. ## Verification - `test/shell.d/plugin-add-test.sh` passes in the VM guest: 7 ok, including a new regression test that stubs `mv` to fail and asse

prs.title: Add graceful low-battery shutdown protection
prs.body: When an awake laptop reaches critically low charge, Omarchy currently warns but can keep running until the battery cuts power. This adds a system battery guard that gives the user a bounded save window and requests normal shutdown while reserve remains. At **5% hardware charge**, or a reported **90 seconds or less remaining**, the guard starts a **60-second countdown**. It updates one notification at the start, 30 seconds, 10 seconds and shutdown. During the last 15 seconds it asks Hyprland windows to close normally so apps can save or show save dialogs. A shorter runtime estimate shortens the deadline to reserve 30 seconds for system shutdown; it never extends the deadline. Poweroff uses the normal systemd transaction without `--force` or application PID kills. - Confirmed charging cancels the countdown, including USB-C/USB-PD supplies. An online adapter that cannot stop discharge does not cancel it. Charging is rechecked before each close request and the final poweroff. - The guard runs while awake before login and after logout. Deadlines and per-window attempts survive daemon restarts; ambiguous dispatch failures are not resent. Missing/invalid percentage cannot pause an establi

prs.body: Reinstalling an unchanged `hyprland` package replaces `/usr/bin/Hyprland`, so the running compositor's `/proc/<pid>/exe` link reads `/usr/bin/Hyprland (deleted)` even though the bytes are identical, and `omarchy-update-restart` asks for a reboot nothing needs. prs.title: Report when a process crashed, not when its core dump finished
prs.body: Fixes #14030. `omarchy-agent-crash` took the prompt's `time:` from the TIME column of `coredumpctl list` (`tail -1 | cut -f1-4`). That goes wrong in two ways: - **TIME is when the dump finished, not when the process crashed.** For a large core that can be a minute later. On this machine a Hermes crash shows `11:49:47` in `coredumpctl list`, but its `COREDUMP_TIMESTAMP` is `11:48:49`. The diagnose-crash skill matches file mtimes to the crash second, so the agent looks in the wrong place. - **The output can end in a notice.** While another `systemd-coredump@.service` is still running, `coredumpctl list` prints `-- Notice: … unit is running, output may be incomplete.` after the table, even with `--no-legend`. `tail -1` then puts `-- Notice: 1 systemd-coredump@.service` into the prompt as the time. It now reads `COREDUMP_TIMESTAMP` from the crash's journal entry (`journalctl -o json -n 1 COREDUMP_PID=<pid> --output-fields=COREDUMP_TIMESTAMP`) and formats it the way `coredumpctl` does (`Thu 2026-10-01 11:48:49 PDT`). prs.title: Scroll with the Steam Deck back buttons
prs.body: ## Summary On a Steam Deck the four back buttons do nothing on the Omarchy desktop. With this change they scroll like a mouse wheel: the upper pair (L4, R4) scrolls up and the lower pair (L5, R5) scrolls down, so either hand can scroll both ways. A press scrolls one notch, and holding a button keeps scrolling. ## Why a helper is needed On the desktop the Deck's controller runs in lizard mode: the firmware drives the pointer from the right trackpad. In that mode the kernel's `hid-steam` driver withholds every gamepad button, back buttons included, from its evdev gamepad device. They only appear after the user holds the ☰ button to switch to gamepad mode, and that switch turns the trackpad pointer off. So nothing on the desktop can see the back buttons while the pointer works. ## How it works - `omarchy-hw-steam-deck` matches the Deck: DMI vendor `Valve` plus product `Jupiter` (LCD) or `Galileo` (OLED). - `omarchy-hw-steam-deck-paddles` (hidden) reads the back buttons from the controller's raw HID reports, the same channel Steam uses. The report layout is taken from `drivers/hid/hid-steam.c`. It scrolls through a uinput virtual mouse wheel, sending `REL_WHEEL` and `REL_WHEEL_HI_RES`.

prs.title: Ignore the duplicate ACPI power button on Chromebooks
prs.body: This PR is fixing an issue I have personally faced. On Chromebooks, pressing the power key flashes the power menu for a moment and closes it again. Each press reaches Hyprland twice, about 22ms apart: once from the EC's `cros_ec_buttons` device and once from the ACPI `Power Button`. `XF86PowerOff` toggles the menu, so the first event opens it and the second closes it. `omarchy-hw-cros-ec-power-key` checks whether a `cros_ec_buttons` device advertises `KEY_POWER` in its sysfs key bitmap. The kernel only registers the buttons the EC says it supports, so this means the EC delivers the key itself. When it does, `default/hypr/input.lua` disables Hyprland's `power-button` device. Machines without a ChromeOS EC never reach that line. The new test runs the detector and the real `input.lua` against fake sysfs trees, including the bitmap captured from the affected machine, an EC with only volume keys, and a regular laptop. It fails without the `input.lua` change. Tested on a Google Craask Chromebook (stock firmware): the menu now stays open, and lock and unlock work. prs.title: Stop treating an initramfs hook banner as a failed rebuild
prs.body: `omarchy-update-analyze-logs` treats pacman's `Updating linux initcpios...` line as proof that mkinitcpio rebuilt an image. That line is the description of `90-mkinitcpio-install.hook`, printed before the hook script decides whether to run mkinitcpio at all. When a `pcsclite`, `p11-kit`, `cryptsetup`, `systemd` or `lvm2` upgrade fires the hook and no preset uses the matching mkinitcpio hook, the script exits without calling mkinitcpio, nothing is built, and the update still ends with: ``` Error: Initramfs generation may have failed. Review logs before restart. ``` That warning is the one signal meant to catch a real initramfs failure before a reboot, and a repeated false alarm teaches people to ignore it. The checker now warns when mkinitcpio reports an error, or when a preset build starts and does not succeed. A hook banner by itself stays quiet. A preset that mkinitcpio skips (`Skipping image`, printed after `Building image from preset`) is not counted as a failed build. One failure comes before any build marker: mkinitcpio sources each preset before printing `Building image from preset`, and dies with `ERROR: Failed to load preset` when the preset is malformed or sources a file

prs.title: Add DisplayLink driver support for USB-C docking stations
prs.body: Docks built around a DisplayLink chip (HP, Dell, Lenovo, Kensington, Plugable, and others) hand their monitors to a userspace driver over USB instead of passing DisplayPort through. It uses the detection helper to distinguish "plug the dock in" from "replug it", since a dock that was already attached has to arrive again before the driver claims it. - **`Install > Service > DisplayLink`** in the menu, following the Install-row convention (`disabled:` on `omarchy-pkg-present displaylink`, no `when:`). - **`manual/33-monitors.md`

prs.title: Offer rootless Docker next to the system daemon
prs.body: Since #8056, `docker` needs `sudo` unless you opt into the docker group, which is root-equivalent. This adds a third way that keeps the protection: a rootless Docker daemon for your user, **next to** the system daemon rather than replacing it. - `docker …` → your rootless daemon: no sudo, no docker group, a container can only reach what your user can. - `sudo docker …` → the system daemon, unchanged: the Windows VM, the Docker TUI behind its prompt, privileged containers, existing workloads. Nothing is migrated and the system daemon is never touched, so it's opt-in and fully reversible. prs.body: Fixes #14130. ## What was wrong `omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy` staged the managed theme colour and then wrote it with `install -T`. `install(1)` unlinks an existing destination before recreating it (`x->unlink_dest_before_opening = true` in coreutils `src/install.c`), so on every theme switch there was a window in which `/etc/<browser>/policies/managed/color.json` did not exist, followed by a window in which it existed but was empty or partial. The staging implied an atomic swap that the final step never performed. prs.title: fix(menu): keep first item flush at originY on initial reveal
prs.body: Fixes #14176 ### Problem When opening a list with more items than fit inside the initial view height (e.g. `SUPER + K` for `omarchy-menu-keybindings`, or any invocation of `omarchy-menu-select` with >8 items), the very first item (index 0) is scrolled up into negative space and clipped. ### Cause On initial layout, `revealCursor()` runs via `Qt.callLater` when `displayModel` loads. Before `resultList.height` settles to the final mapped window height, `overhang` evaluates to `> 0` because `item.y + item.height + reach` exceeds the initial list height. This sets `resultList.contentY = overhang`. Because `root.selectedIndex === 0`, the underhang branch (`if (root.selectedIndex > 0)`) never runs to reset `contentY` back to `originY`. ### Solution Guard `revealCursor()` so that when `root.selectedIndex === 0`, `resultList.contentY` is explicitly kept flush at `resultList.originY`.

prs.title: Allow slow OpenClaw dashboard probes

prs.title: Open imv at 80% of the monitor instead of the shared 875x600 float
prs.body: ## Problem imv is in the shared `floating-window` tag, so every image opens in the same 875x600 float as the small terminals and dialogs. Most images people open are screenshots and photos at full screen resolution (a 4K Omarchy screenshot is 3840x2160), so they show up as a thumbnail and the window has to be resized by hand every time. A per-app `size` rule for imv can't override this from user config either, because the tag's 875x600 wins over it. The user has to remove the tag first (`tag = "-floating-window"`) and then re-add float/center/size, which is not obvious. ## Fix Take imv out of the shared tag and give it its own float, center and size rules, the same way `org.omarchy.about` does: centered at 80% of the monitor (`(monitor_w*0.8)` / `(monitor_h*0.8)`), so it scales with any resolution and display scale. Still floating, still opaque (the media opacity rule is unchanged). ## Testing Hyprland 0.56.2, 3840x2160 monitor: applied the equivalent rules live with `hyprctl eval` and opened a screenshot in imv. The window opened floating and centered at 3072x1728 instead of 875x600. `luac -p` passes on the changed file. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](

prs.title: Avoid double scaling Ghostty text
prs.body: Fixes #14221. `omarchy display text size 16` writes 12pt to every terminal and sets the GTK text multiplier to 1.3636. Ghostty applies that multiplier again, making its text larger than Foot, Kitty and Alacritty. Divide Ghostty's configured font size by the effective GTK multiplier, and include that multiplier when reporting its apparent point size. Read the setting back after updates so failed GTK set/reset operations still use the factor actually in effect. Read the previous GTK factor before making changes, then confirm the effective value after updating it. A failed read returns an error before shell or terminal config updates; a failed readback restores the previous GTK multiplier. An unsuccessful rollback is explicitly reported. Reporting shows `n/a` when the apparent size cannot be determined. Other terminals keep their existing point-size mapping. Known limitation from the final review: GTK rollback restores the effective multiplier; if the key was previously unset, it leaves that value explicitly set instead of restoring the unset state. ### Validation - Regression covers every accepted size, multiple GTK interface-font sizes, repeated changes, reset, failed settings write

prs.title: Refresh the bar clock immediately across system suspend and resume
prs.body: Fixes #14247 ## Problem After waking from suspend or opening a laptop lid, the bar clock (`omarchy.clock`) stays on the pre-suspend minute until Quickshell's scheduled timer elapses (a lag of up to ~60 seconds). `SystemClock` in Quickshell schedules its minute update via a one-shot `QTimer` using `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, which freezes during suspend. When the system wakes, the remaining monotonic delay must elapse before `dateChanged` triggers. ## Solution 1. Add a wall-clock sleep watcher `Timer` in `shell/plugins/panels/clock/BarWidget.qml` that samples `Date.now()`. When a time gap greater than 2500ms is detected (system sleep, lid close/open, or clock adjustment), it immediately calls `root.refresh()` to update `displayDate = new Date()` and refreshes the calendar popup if opened. 2. In `bin/omarchy-system-wake`, trigger a non-blocking `omarchy-shell -q omarchy.clock refresh` on wake. ## Validation - Added assertions in `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` verifying that `BarWidget.qml` defines `sleepWatch` to refresh the clock across suspend and that `omarchy-system-wake` triggers clock refresh. - Ran `bash ./test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` (all 136 assertions passed).

prs.title: Animate background reveal across all screens in multi-monitor setups
prs.body: Closes #14065 ### Problem On multi-monitor setups, background reveals (from wallpaper or theme transitions) only animated on the first monitor whose `incomingFrame` finished loading. Because all screens share a single `revealAnimation`, the first screen to finish loaded started the animation (advancing `revealProgress > 0`), causing later screens to see `revealProgress !== 0` in `maybeStartReveal()` and return immediately. As a result, `panel.maskReady` remained `false` on those other screens, so they never rendered the slanted wipe and instead cut abruptly to the new background only after the full 420 ms animation concluded. ### Solution - Track ready panels for each `backgroundVersion` via `readyPanels`. - Start the shared reveal when all screen panels report ready (`readyPanels >= Quickshell.screens.length`), or upon a 250 ms fallback timeout (`revealWaitTimer`) so theme colors and wallpaper reveals are not delayed by an unusually slow screen. - Allow slower screens that finish loading while the reveal animation is underway (`root.revealProgress < 1`) to set `maskReady = true` via `root.panelReady(panel)` and seamlessly join the in-flight reveal animation instead of cutting at c

prs.title: Bind backgroundVersion on base BackgroundMedia to bust cache on same-name theme switches
prs.body: Closes #14191 ### Problem When switching between two themes that share an identical wallpaper filename (such as `1-moon.png` or `omarchy.png`), both resolve to the same durable path (`~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/backgrounds/...`). While the transition frames animate the change from the temporary snapshots, once the transition completes, `BackgroundMedia` (`base`) re-evaluates the durable path. Because `base` did not bind `version: root.backgroundVersion`, `BackgroundMedia` generated an unversioned `file://` URL and Qt's image cache reused the pixmap from the previous theme, snapping back to the old wallpaper. ### Solution - In `shell/plugins/background/Background.qml`, bind `version: root.backgroundVersion` and `cached: true` on `base` (`BackgroundMedia`). `BackgroundMedia` includes `?v=<version>` in its `imageUrl` when `version > 0`, properly cache-busting same-path file replacements across theme transitions. - Clear cached `nativeSizes[finalPath]` on forced transitions so new dimensions are reprobed. - Added unit test assertion in `test/shell.d/background-test.sh`. ### Validation Ran `bash ./test/shell.d/background-test.sh` (all tests passed).

prs.body: ## Why Closing a laptop's lid suspends it unless an external monitor is attached. prs.title: Stop orphaned speed-test transfers after supervisor exit
prs.body: If the speed-test supervisor is killed before its EXIT cleanup finishes, its download/upload workers can keep saturating the connection indefinitely. This happened twice on a phone hotspot, with downloads still running at about 18.7 MB/s after the supervisor had exited. Give each traffic worker its own process group and keep its watchdog and transfer processes in that group. The watchdog checks both the supervisor and worker while a transfer is in progress, so SIGKILL also stops a blocked curl or upload pipeline. Normal cleanup signals whole worker groups instead of racing individual child lookups against the next transfer. The offline regression runs the real command with stubbed routing, curl, and dd. It checks SIGTERM and SIGKILL during blocked downloads and uploads, and verifies that no live process remains in the test session. Unchanged upstream fails the SIGKILL case with eight workers and eight transfers left running; all four cases pass with this patch. No real speed tests or internet transfers were used for verification. Related: #11054 proposes the same process-group/watchdog approach; #14026 and #11235 check the parent between transfers. prs.title: Bound wallpaper resource use when sampling bar colors
prs.body: Fixes #14167. ## Problem The transparent bar samples its wallpaper through ImageMagick. The existing `[0]` selector bounds multi-frame backgrounds, but a single highly compressed, high-resolution image still expands at source size before the resize. ImageMagick's default memory limit follows available RAM and its disk cache is unlimited; on Omarchy `/tmp` is normally tmpfs. A sandboxed 7900×5000 RGB PNG (125 KiB on disk) made the current helper peak at 641,236 KiB RSS just to choose between two configured colors. ## Change Bound this best-effort sample to: - 256 MiB of ImageMagick pixel-cache memory with map and disk spill disabled - two ImageMagick threads - five seconds, with an external process-group timeout When a wallpaper cannot be sampled inside those bounds, the helper uses its existing configured text-color fallback. The new regression executes the real helper with stubbed `timeout` and `magick`, checks every bound and still verifies the sampled color controls the contrast choice. ## Testing - `test/shell.d/bar-text-color-test.sh`: 5/5 - `./test/cli`: 117/117 - Base mutation: new bounds assertion fails - `bash -n`, ShellCheck, `git diff --check`: pass - Bubblewrap, 7900×50

prs.title: Tell logind when the session locks
prs.body: ## Summary The lock never tells logind about itself: `LockedHint` stays `no` while locked, and no `Lock` signal goes out. Programs that watch logind can't see the lock. KeePassXC, for example, locks its databases on the `Lock` signal, so on Omarchy it stays unlocked. See also #9076. Send `Session.Lock()` when a lock is requested. Set `LockedHint` while the session lock is secure, and clear it on unlock. At startup, clear a hint left by a shell that died locked. Both calls go through `busctl` with `--allow-interactive-authorization=no`; logind lets the session owner make them without polkit. Any process in the session can set `LockedHint` (see #11196), but here a spoofed hint can only make listeners lock early. The `1password --lock` case in `omarchy-system-lock` (#7785) is unchanged. The shell still ignores logind's `Lock` signal, so `loginctl lock-session` does nothing; that's a separate change. ## Validation - `bash test/shell.d/lock-login-session-test.sh` passes (new), as do the other lock tests. - `git diff --check` passes. - Live on 4.0.4 with the same patch: `Lock` at the request, `LockedHint` true when secure and false at unlock, KeePassXC locked. prs.title: Reset media bar marquee when the label stops scrolling
prs.body: ## Problem The media bar widget sometimes shows a blank label, or only the tail of it (e.g. `· Artist`), while the popup shows the track correctly. A shell restart clears it until the next track change. Two paths leave the marquee's `labelText.x` off zero: 1. **A title that grows but still fits.** `scrollClip.width` is `min(maxLabelWidth, implicitWidth)`, and `needsScroll` compared `implicitWidth` against it. When the label widens, `needsScroll` re-evaluates before the clip catches up, so it reads `true` for one binding pass. The animation starts, sets `x` to `from` (the old clip width), and stops on the next pass, leaving the label pushed out of view. Going from a 143.75px label to a 165.31px one lands at `x = 143.75`: nothing visible. 2. **A long title replaced by one that fits.** `needsScroll` flips to `false`, the animation stops, and `x` stays wherever it was mid-scroll. The existing reset only fired under reduced motion. ## Fix - Compare `needsScroll` against `root.maxLabelWidth`. At steady state this is equivalent (`implicitWidth > min(cap, implicitWidth)` ⇔ `implicitWidth > cap`), but it never flips for a title that fits. - Reset `x` to 0 whenever the animation stops, not o

It also catches bluetoothctl's printed failures when its exit status is zero, checks Paired and Connected state, and skips a redundant connection request when pairing already established the connection. Disconnect and forget failures are surfaced too; forgetting an already disconnected device still works. Found while investigating an AirPods Pro pairing failure. Direct BlueZ pairing later succeeded, but the original failure's cause is not established; this PR addresses the confirmed suppressed-error behavior and does not replace the Bluetooth transport or add AirPods-specific handling. prs.title: screensaver: kill socat when focus-restore waiter exits
prs.body: ## Problem `omarchy-launch-screensaver` opens Hyprland's event socket through a background `socat` process substitution. When the script finishes, the read end closes, but `socat` stays alive until the next Hyprland event. That write hits a closed pipe and logs `Broken pipe` (see #14318). The screensaver itself still works. ## Fix Capture `socat_pid=$!` after the process substitution, and `trap 'kill "$socat_pid" 2>/dev/null' EXIT` only inside the focus-restore waiter subshell. That kills `socat` when the waiter exits, without attaching a trap to the main script's EXIT path. ## Tests - `test/shell.d/screensaver-socat-cleanup-test.sh`: socat stays alive while the launcher returns, then is gone after the focus-restore waiter exits. Fail-first with the kill trap removed fails as expected. - `test/shell.d/screensaver-workspace-test.sh` still passes. Fixes #14318

prs.title: Stop the screensaver event listener after cleanup
prs.body: Fixes #14318. `omarchy-launch-screensaver` opens Hyprland's event socket before launching terminal windows, then leaves a background watcher using that stream so focus can return to the original monitor after the last screensaver closes. When the watcher finished, it closed its read descriptor but did not stop the `socat` producer. The next Hyprland event made `socat` write into the closed pipe, print `Broken pipe`, and exit. I kept the existing listener and focus behavior. The launcher now records the process-substitution PID and gives the background watcher an EXIT trap that stops that exact process after focus restoration finishes. This avoids killing the listener when the foreground launcher exits, which would break the existing background focus watcher. The focused regression extends `screensaver-workspace-test.sh`. On unmodified `quattro`, it failed with: ``` socat pid 2064656 is still running not ok - the Hyprland event listener stops after focus is restored ``` With this change, all seven assertions pass. The test also confirms the listener remains available while multiple screensavers close and that focus still returns correctly. Bash syntax checks, ShellCheck at warning s

prs.title: Make brightness keys work on external displays with a kernel backlight
prs.body: With an Apple Studio Display focused, the brightness keys show the OSD but the screen doesn't change. Today they go through `sudo asdcontrol`, and Studio Display firmware 17.0 ignores that command (macOS behaves the same). ## What this changes Some kernels expose an external display's brightness as a regular backlight device on its connector, for example `dcp-DP-3-bl` with [aurora-linux#15]( (still open). When the focused external display has one, the brightness keys now use that kernel backlight instead of asdcontrol: brightnessctl, the usual step sizes, the OSD, and no sudo. Everything else works as it does today: - Displays without a connector backlight (every display on a stock kernel, DDC monitors, Studio Displays on older kernels) take the existing path. - Laptop screens keep `omarchy-hw-display`'s choice. Some GPU drivers attach a backlight to the internal connector that isn't the one driving the panel (gmux on dual-GPU Macs), so internal connectors aren't checked. - Only a connected connector's backlight is used, so a disconnected connector with the same name on another card can't be picked by mistake. - If more than one connected connector has the monitor's name (for examp

prs.title: Install Zed from upstream when the repo has no zed package
prs.body: ## Summary Fixes #12625. `omarchy install editor zed` runs `omarchy-pkg-add zed omazed` as one pacman transaction. On aarch64 the omarchy repo publishes `omazed` (arch=any) but no `zed` package, so pacman aborts the whole transaction and neither Zed nor omazed gets installed. ## What changed - `bin/omarchy-install-editor-zed`: if `pacman -Si zed` resolves, keep the existing `omarchy-pkg-add zed omazed` transaction (x86_64 behaviour unchanged). Otherwise install `omazed` on its own and fall back to Zed's official installer (` which ships aarch64 Linux builds. `omazed setup` and the launch step are unchanged. - `test/shell.d/zed-install-test.sh`: new test covering both paths (repo package available vs. unavailable) with stubbed `pacman`, `omarchy-pkg-add` and `curl`. - `test/shell.d/desktop-entry-launch-test.sh`: stub `pacman` so the existing installer launch test keeps exercising the package path. ## Testing - `bash test/shell.d/zed-install-test.sh`: 2 ok - `bash test/shell.d/desktop-entry-launch-test.sh`: all ok - `bash -n` and `shellcheck` on the changed script: clean
